newsitem.title: UK: Talk of EMU delay no catastrophe-Bundesbank member.
newsitem.headline: Talk of EMU delay no catastrophe-Bundesbank member.

text.p: A member of the German Bundesbank's powerful council said on Tuesday it would not be catastrophic to discuss postponing the introduction of a single European currency.

Hans-Juergen Koebnick was speaking after the German government retreated from a controversial plan to revalue the central bank's gold reserves as a means of easing Germany's entry into the single currency in 1999.
Koebnick said he had always objected to the view that it would be a catastrophe to to discuss postponement.
"That is not the case," he told BBC television. "One has to work it out -- look at the pros and cons."

German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said earlier that he and Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer had struck a compromise deal under which windfall profits from the gold revaluation would not be transferred to the Bonn government until next year.
But Tietmeyer said later that a final deal had not been struck.
